page: Microsoft Azure E128ps_v7 is an ARM-based memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server features 128 dedicated vCPUs built on 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) paired with 1024.0 GB of system memory, providing a uniform ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external attached storage such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent file systems, nor does it feature dedicated GPU accelerators.

The ARM processor architecture delivers high core density and power efficiency across high-concurrency environments. With 128 dedicated cores and one terabyte of memory, the instance is structured to prevent resource contention among high-volume threads. However, without built-in local NVMe drives, all disk I/O operations rely entirely on remote network storage interfaces, which makes external storage network configuration a primary architectural factor for performance.

From an operational and cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides favorable compute and memory density compared to traditional x86 alternatives, though it requires workloads compiled specifically for ARM execution environments. The combination of 1024 GB RAM and 128 vCPUs makes Microsoft Azure E128ps_v7 well suited for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching layers, distributed analytics engines, and enterprise memory-intensive workloads that utilize remote persistent block volumes.
description: Microsoft Azure E128ps_v7 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned with 128 dedicated arm64 vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of RAM. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation (8.0 GB per core), engineered for data-heavy and memory-intensive enterprise tasks. The instance does not bundle local disk storage, directing all disk activity to remote storage volumes like Azure Premium Storage, and contains no hardware GPU accelerators. The use of dedicated ARM64 cores delivers scalable compute density and favorable resource efficiency for multithreaded operations. Workloads must maintain compatibility with ARM binaries. Given its large memory capacity and dedicated multi-core compute profile, this virtual machine functions effectively for in-memory databases, large caching clusters, distributed data processing, and large-scale analytics platforms requiring substantial memory allocations alongside high processor counts.
